creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`commands.md` requirement #5 is already "Commands should be optional", the motivating example is `hm`, and a `command default:` sketch exists with routing and help worked out. The design risk is largely retired; this is implementation.

What it costs today: `remind:628-629` records "Manual dispatch: rad command blocks can't coexist with a default action" and then hand-rolls ~150 lines of switch, per-command arity checks, manual `parse_int` of ids, and manual cross-validation of `--repeat`. `devenv:305` (890 runs) and `laptop:120` carry the identical comment verbatim and lose ~25 lines each. `dot:100-102` says it in older words. `addpath` uses `--list`/`--remove` flags for the same reason.

`hm` is the sharp one: the design doc's own motivating script uses flags in reality, while the `rad docs examples/hm` tutorial rewrites it with commands and changes the UX to do so (`hm tar` becomes `hm show tar`).

Collides with in-flight main-board work - RAD-394 (nested command definitions) is in progress and RAD-393 (sub commands) is next. Sequence deliberately rather than starting cold.

Related and unresolved: dev-longtail argues commands shouldn't be mutually exclusive at all, since 14 dispatcher-shaped dev scripts use boolean flags as composable verbs with an implied pipeline order (`cron-ai/dev:5`: "Actions are composable: `./dev -lft` runs lint, format, and test"). That contradicts `commands.md:155` and `:488` outright. The report rates it high confidence on the problem and low-to-medium on the direction, and flags the composability diagnosis as its own inference. A default command can proceed regardless, but multi-command would ripple through routing, help generation and default-command semantics.

---

### Design doc, verified

`docs/thinking/commands.md` exists (19K). Everything the card cites is really there:

- **Requirement #5** is at line 369, in the 2025-10-05 requirements list: "**Commands should be optional** - tool can work with or without them". An earlier 2025-07-08 list says the same at line 294.
- **The `command default:` sketch** is at lines 373-423, under "### Default Commands", motivated by `hm` exactly as the card says (`hm grep` == `hm view grep`). It appears again in the fuller single-file example at line 547.
- **The proposed semantics** are spelled out at lines 417-421: `command default:` is optional; if defined, `tool <args>` routes to it; if not defined, `tool` with no command errors listing available commands; `default` becomes a boolean like other commands; `tool -h` shows all commands plus the default's args.
- **The mutual-exclusivity claims** the card says dev-longtail contradicts are at line 155 ("'else' not required because commands are mutually exclusive anyway") and line 488 ("The check `if aaa and ddd:` is logically impossible since commands are mutually exclusive"). Both verified verbatim.
- **The conclusions section** (lines 628-655) lists `command default:` under "Possible direction for v1" and leaves command routing as an explicit open question.

**One thing the doc is stale on, and it matters here.** The sketch routes with top-level booleans - `if default:` / `if edit:`. That is *not* what shipped. Commands today dispatch through a `calls` line naming a function or an inline lambda (see `SYNTAX.md`, "Script Commands"). The doc's own open-questions list flags this as undecided ("Function delegation: whether to add `command add: calls do_add` syntax, or just rely on manual delegation"); `calls` won. So take requirement #5 and the motivating example from the doc, but design the default command against the `calls` model, not the boolean model. The sketch's "`default` becomes a boolean like other commands" no longer maps onto anything.

### Orientation

Commands are registered as CLI flags in `core/runner.go` and dispatched there:

- `registerCommands` (line 518) iterates `r.scriptData.Commands`, builds an `ra.NewCmd(scriptCmd.ExternalName)` per command, registers script-level `args:` on it as `AsScriptFlagOnly` and the command's own args as `AsCommandArg`, then `RRootCmd.RegisterCmd(raSubCmd)` returns a `*bool` "was used" pointer stored in `r.cmdInvocations`.
- `parseAndExecute` (around line 448) calls `RRootCmd.ParseOrExit`, scans `r.cmdInvocations` for the first entry whose `*inv.usedPtr` is true, and if commands exist but none was invoked emits `RP.UsageErrorExit("Must specify a command")` at line 462 - unless `--help`/`--version`/`--src`/`--cst-tree`/`--ast-tree` is set. **Line 462 is the exact behavior this card replaces**: instead of erroring, route to the default command.
- The invoked command's args go to `interpreter.InitArgs(commandArgs)` at line 480.

Upstream of that: `rts/converter.go` `convertCmdBlock` builds `rl.CmdBlock` (`rts/rl/ast_types.go`), `rts/check/binder.go` `bindFile`/`visitCmdBlock` binds command args and resolves callbacks, and `core/command_types.go` `FromCmdBlock` converts to the runtime `ScriptCommand`. Name hyphenation goes through `rts.ToExternalName` (`rts/name_transform.go:7`).

Arg registration modes are in `core/args.go` - `AsScriptFlagOnly`, `AsCommandArg`, `AsGlobalFlag`. A default command needs its args accepted as bare positionals at the top level, which is a mode question: today only a sub-command's args are positional.

Note the AGENTS.md constraint: **`rts` must not import `core`**. The AST and checker know nothing about `ra`.

### Sequencing - read this before starting

The nested-commands card in this column (`Support nested and sub commands`) has **uncommitted work sitting in worktree `/Users/amterp/src/rad4`** that rewrites `registerCommands` into a recursive `registerCommandTree` and replaces the first-used-command scan with a `resolveInvokedCommand` that descends to the deepest invoked command. It touches every line cited above. That branch has zero commits and is 81 behind `main`.

Starting this card against `main` guarantees a painful merge. Land the nested work first, or at minimum read `git diff --cached` in `/Users/amterp/src/rad4` and build on its shape. The two features also interact semantically: rad4 currently errors on a bare namespace invocation (`Must specify a command for 'remote'`), which is precisely the hole a *namespace-level* default command would fill. Decide whether `command default:` is top-level only or allowed inside a namespace, and say so on this card.

### Where to start

- `core/runner.go:448-480` - the dispatch block, and line 462 in particular.
- `core/runner.go:518-565` - `registerCommands`.
- `core/args.go` - the arg-registration modes.
- `core/command_types.go` - `ScriptCommand`, `FromCmdBlock`.
- `/Users/amterp/src/rad4` - `git diff --cached core/runner.go` for the nested-commands rewrite of the same code.
- `docs/thinking/commands.md:373-423` - the design sketch.
- `SYNTAX.md`, "Script Commands" section - what actually shipped.
- The grammar rule is `cmd_block` in `~/src/tree-sitter-rad/grammar.js`. Whether `default` needs grammar support depends on the syntax chosen - `command default:` parses as an ordinary command name today, so a purely semantic treatment may need no grammar change at all. Confirm that before assuming a grammar release is on the critical path.
- Check `docs/red/` for an existing RED on commands before revisiting settled ground; a decision this size probably warrants a new one.

### How to verify

Build is `make build`, producing `bin/radd`. A bare `rad` is the installed release and will not have your changes.

```sh
make build
go test ./core/testing/... ./rts/... ./radls/lstesting/...
```

Snapshot suites:

- `core/testing/snapshots/args/` - end-to-end runs including command dispatch and usage strings. Regenerate the relevant file with `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=args/cmds` (substitute the real path substring for the file you add). The `=` is required; a bare `-update -run X` swallows `-run` as the update value.
- `rts/check/snapshots/` - checker diagnostics. `go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots -update=commands`.

Manual smoke test:

```sh
./bin/radd /tmp/hm.rad grep          # routes to default
./bin/radd /tmp/hm.rad edit grep     # routes to edit
./bin/radd /tmp/hm.rad -h            # lists commands AND the default's args
./bin/radd /tmp/hm.rad               # default with no args - decide and lock the behavior
```

### Done when

- A script with `command default:` routes bare args to it; a script without one still errors listing available commands (the current line-462 behavior, preserved).
- `tool -h` shows both the command list and the default command's args, per the design doc's stated help behavior.
- Ambiguity is resolved deterministically and tested: a default command taking a positional `page`, invoked as `tool edit` where `edit` is also a command name. Which wins, and is it explainable? This is the sharpest correctness question on the card - write a snapshot case for it.
- `rad check` rejects the incoherent cases: two `default` commands, a `default` command with no `calls`, a default arg colliding with a script-level arg name.
- Snapshot coverage in `core/testing/snapshots/args/` and `rts/check/snapshots/`.
- `SYNTAX.md` documents it, and `docs-web/docs/guide/script-commands.md` matches.
- `make verify-generated` is clean - CI runs it.
- Per AGENTS.md, invoke the Rad Docs Maintainer subagent - this is user-facing syntax.
- If this changes how existing scripts behave, it is a breaking change and needs all three migration layers per AGENTS.md: a migration diagnostic (prefer static detection in `rts/check/`), an error doc under `core/error_docs/`, and an entry in `docs-web/docs/migrations/v0.X.md`. Commit prefix `feat!:`.

### Watch out for

- **Do not resurrect the boolean routing model** from the doc's sketch. `calls` shipped; `if default:` did not.
- **Do not start this in parallel with the nested-commands work.** They rewrite the same 40 lines.
- **`rad`'s own subcommands are Rad scripts** in `core/embedded/` (`check`, `docs`, `new`, `stash`, `explain`, ...). Command-dispatch changes can break `rad` itself. Smoke-test each one after the change: `./bin/radd check --help`, `./bin/radd docs --help`, and so on.
- **Error codes are banded and never reused** (`rts/rl/errors.go`; 4xxxx for validation/lint). Any new diagnostic needs a fresh number plus a user-facing doc at `core/error_docs/<code>.md`.
- **The composability question stays out of scope.** The card records dev-longtail's argument that commands should not be mutually exclusive at all, rated low-to-medium confidence with the diagnosis flagged as its own inference. A default command is orthogonal to it. If multi-command dispatch ever lands it will reopen default-command semantics, but do not pre-solve it here.
- **Docs snippets are executed by tests** (`core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go`), so any example you add to the guide has to actually run.

### Addendum - two things probed directly (2026-08-10)

**1. No grammar change is needed.** `command default:` already parses today as an ordinary command named `default`. Verified against `main` with a freshly built `bin/radd`: `rad check` reports no diagnostics, and `./bin/radd script.rad default grep` runs the callback and prints `default page=grep`. So `tree-sitter-rad` is **not** on this card's critical path - no grammar edit, no grammar release, no `replace` directive dance. The work is purely semantic, in `core/runner.go`. That is a meaningful reduction against the `xl` sizing.

**2. The motivating case does not reach the code this card was scoped around, and the real fix is probably upstream in `ra`.** There are two distinct failure paths today, and they fire in different layers:

```
# no args at all
$ ./bin/radd tool.rad
Must specify a command                          <- core/runner.go:462, the runner's own check

# a bare positional, i.e. the `hm grep` case
$ ./bin/radd tool.rad grep
Too many positional arguments. Unused: [grep]   <- ra, during RRootCmd.ParseOrExit
```

The second one is the `hm grep` case from the design doc - the whole point of the card - and it **never reaches line 462**. `ra` rejects the unconsumed positional during parsing, before the runner gets a chance to route anything. So "replace the `Must specify a command` branch with a default route" is necessary but not sufficient; it only fixes the no-args case.

Making `tool <args>` route to a default command requires `ra` to stop treating a trailing positional as an error when a default command is registered - which is a change in `~/src/ra`, not here. Per AGENTS.md, `ra` is first-party and the right fix goes upstream rather than being worked around in Rad. **Scope the `ra` change before estimating this card.** It is the same shape as the shared-args help gap on the nested-commands card: the interesting work is in the arg library, not the interpreter.
title: Add a default command
